record.original_question: Can one develop a theory of general fractional integrals and general fractional derivatives on conventional function spaces beyond the spaces treated in the paper, in particular on L^p spaces and on Holder weighted spaces?

evidence.quote: Develop a theory of the GFIs and GFDs on other conventional spaces of functions including Lp and Holder weighted spaces.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Let $\kappa:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ be a Sonine kernel, i.e. a locally integrable function for which there exists an associated kernel $k$ such that
$$\int_0^t \kappa(t-\tau)\,k(\tau)\,d\tau = 1, \qquad t>0.$$
For such a pair $(\kappa,k)$, define the general fractional integral (GFI) and the general fractional derivatives (GFD) of Riemann–Liouville and Caputo type, respectively, by
$$(\mathbb{I}_{(\kappa)} f)(t) = \int_0^t \kappa(t-\tau) f(\tau)\,d\tau,$$
$$(\mathbb{D}_{(k)} f)(t) = \frac{d}{dt}\int_0^t k(t-\tau) f(\tau)\,d\tau, \qquad ({}_*\mathbb{D}_{(k)} f)(t) = \int_0^t k(t-\tau) f'(\tau)\,d\tau.$$
Recall the classical weighted Hölder space $H_0^{\lambda,\mu}([a,b])$ (functions $f$ with $(t-a)^\mu f(t)$ Hölder continuous of order $\lambda$ vanishing at $a$) and the Lebesgue spaces $L^p([a,b])$, $1\le p\le\infty$, on which the Riemann–Liouville fractional integrals and derivatives have a well-developed mapping theory.

Problem. Develop a corresponding theory of the general fractional integrals $\mathbb{I}_{(\kappa)}$ and the general fractional derivatives $\mathbb{D}_{(k)}$, ${}_*\mathbb{D}_{(k)}$ with Sonine kernels acting on:
(i) the Lebesgue spaces $L^p([a,b])$, $1\le p\le\infty$;
(ii) the weighted Hölder spaces $H_0^{\lambda,\mu}([a,b])$.

Specifically, identify natural subclasses of Sonine kernels for which $\mathbb{I}_{(\kappa)}$, $\mathbb{D}_{(k)}$, and ${}_*\mathbb{D}_{(k)}$ are bounded operators on these spaces, characterize their ranges, establish the corresponding fundamental theorems of general fractional calculus in this functional-analytic setting, and obtain mapping properties that parallel the classical Hardy–Littlewood and Hölder-space theorems for the Riemann–Liouville operators.
artifact.category_tag: general fractional calculus on function spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys on general fractional integrals/derivatives with Sonine kernels (e.g., Luchko 2021–2023) explicitly list the development of a theory on $L^p$ and Hölder weighted spaces as an important open direction. While the theory has been advanced on spaces of continuous functions, on functions with integrable singularity at zero, on a finite interval, and via multi-kernel and operational-calculus extensions, no comprehensive mapping theory analogous to the Riemann–Liouville case on $L^p$ or weighted Hölder spaces appears to have been established.

status_evidence.title: The General Fractional Integrals and Derivatives on a Finite Interval
status_evidence.snippet: An important topic for further research would be to develop a theory of the left- and right-sided general fractional integrals and derivatives on a finite interval on Hölder spaces or weighted L^p-spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The development of a theory of GFIs/GFDs on Hölder and weighted L^p spaces is identified as an open direction for further research.

status_evidence.title: General Fractional Integrals and Derivatives with the Sonine Kernels
status_evidence.snippet: General fractional integrals and derivatives with Sonine kernels are studied on spaces of functions continuous on the positive real semi-axis with an integrable singularity at the origin.
status_evidence.claim: Existing theory has been built on continuous-function spaces with singularity at 0, not on L^p or weighted Hölder spaces.

status_evidence.title: Extension of Luchko operational calculus to multi-kernel general fractional derivatives
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work extends the Luchko operational calculus from single-kernel to multi-kernel general fractional derivatives.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent extensions focus on operational calculus and multi-kernel cases rather than on L^p or Hölder mapping properties.
